newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-BT, C&W seen lifting yr profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-BT, C&W seen lifting yr profits.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc and Cable and Wireless are set to show healthy profits when they release full-year figures in the coming days.
Analysts are expecting BT to post annual pretax profits of some 3.2 billion pounds compared to 3.02 billion in 1995/96 when the company reports on Thursday.
But BT's Q4 earnings will be reined because of a 50 million stg revenue loss, partly due to fewer working days in the period.
C&W pre-tax profits for the year to end-March, due out on Wednesday, are forecast in a range of 1.325 to 1.4 billion stg, excluding exceptional items. That compares with 1.262 billion stg a year ago.
BT, which has shed around 115,000 jobs since privatisation in 1984, is expected to announce a redundancy charge of 350-365 million stg.
"Excluding these factors, we estimate three percent underlying pre-tax profit growth for the quarter with a heavy impact from the timing of price reductions," says brokers Lehman Brothers.
However, key volume numbers are expected to be steady in the last quarter. Volume growth in inland calls is expected to come in at seven percent and international calls at eight percent.

After a landslide election victory swept the Labour Party to power last week, some analysts are already anticipating a windfall tax on BT worth 1.5-2.0 billion stg, to be announced with Labour's first budget.

But the company, which expects clearance in autumn for its $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications Corp has seen its shares rise further since the former Conservative government's crushing defeat on May 1.
There is speculation that Labour will move promptly to lift broadcasting restrictions on BT -- possibly in return for free "superhighway" services to schools.
C&W unit Hongkong Telecom on Thursday announced 1996/97 net profits of $1.4 billion, a 12.5 percent rise.
Hongkong Telecom accounted for over 40 percent of C&W group turnover in 1995/96. C&W owns almost 60 percent of Hongkong Telecom.
